topic: Simple Electric Circuits and Household Wiring
key_concepts: A simple electric circuit is made of a dry cell, bulb, wires, and switch.
The dry cell supplies electrical energy to the circuit.
The bulb is the load that lights when electric current flows.
Connecting wires provide a path for electricity.
A switch opens and closes the circuit.
Closing the switch completes the circuit and the bulb lights.
Opening the switch breaks the circuit and the bulb turns off.
Removing or loosening the bulb opens the circuit and stops current.
Disconnecting the dry cell stops the circuit from working.
Household wiring connects from the meter to different parts of the house.
Electrical symbols are used to draw circuit diagrams.
House wiring contains several simple circuits that supply appliances.
